summary: Tested new Visual Studio feature end-to-end. Backend: all 5 template generations (/api/ai/visual: quote, tweet, infographic, carousel, slideshow) pass with valid non-empty data structures via pytest. Frontend: /visuals route loads, all 5 templates generate copy and render inside [data-testid=visual-canvas] (no placeholder text), theme switching works (chalkboard/whiteboard/midnight/gradient), carousel prev/next/play navigation works, PNG download triggers and completes, and 'Use in post' exports the PNG and navigates to /composer with mediaUrl + prefilled content (verified visually in composer).

issues: html-to-image logs non-fatal SecurityError warnings when parsing cross-origin Google Fonts stylesheets (fonts.googleapis.com). Download still succeeds. Optional: preload/self-host the Inter font or set skipFonts:true / fontEmbedCSS option in toPng() to silence these warnings and guarantee correct font embedding in the exported PNG.

action_items: Optional polish: pass {skipFonts:true} or provide fontEmbedCSS to html-to-image toPng() calls in Visuals.jsx to eliminate the non-fatal CSSStyleSheet cross-origin console warnings and ensure font fidelity in exported PNG.
critical_code_review_comments: Visuals.jsx: generate() catch block silently swallows the error object; consider logging err for easier debugging.
Autoplay interval loops through slides.length + 1 which is correct (cover + slides), but there is no cleanup when user clicks prev/next during playing — minor UX nit.
toPng() called twice in useInPost/download without a shared helper — small DRY opportunity.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Visual Studio feature fully working. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_visuals.py covers all 5 templates. Only cosmetic issue is html-to-image warnings for cross-origin Google Fonts CSS which do not block export.
